text:
Erik Karlsson's time in Pittsburgh looks to be running out. Markerzone relayed that Penguins beat reporter Josh Yohe says Karlsson and Rickard Rakell are about to be traded, and Ottawa and Montreal have both come up in the speculation. The Senators would be a homecoming for the defenseman who won his first two Norris Trophies there.

The results lately are rough. Karlsson has no goals and four assists in his last ten games, against about 8.5 points we would expect at his ice time, and the Penguins have lost eight of those ten. With him on the ice at five on five, they get about 47% of the expected goals and do eight points worse than without him.

Some of that is bad luck. Pittsburgh has scored 6.9 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him out there, which is why our talent range for his scoring sits close to where he is now even after the cold stretch. At 36 he still plays 23 minutes, and last season Evolving-Hockey had him 23rd of 215 defensemen against top competition, while Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking put his shot assists in the 98th percentile. A contender would be buying that passer, and hoping the bounces follow him.
